examples.en: Excuse me, who's next?

note: The answer: «Ја сам» - I am.

examples.en: Do you have anything smaller?

note: A request for smaller bills or coins; the answer is often «Немам, извините».

key: phr:опростите, да ли бисте могли да ми помогнете
meanings: excuse me, could you help me

examples.sr: [О̀простите, да ли бисте мо̏гли да ми по̀могнете]?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you help me?

note: A polite request to a passer-by; «опростите» gets their attention.

meanings: I can't find my way, I'm lost

examples.sr: [Не мо̀гу да се сна̏ђем], где је станица?
examples.en: I can't find my way around, where is the station?
A bit slower, please, I don't understand.

examples.sr: Видимо се кад се вратиш - [сре̏ћан пу̑т]!
examples.en: See you when you get back - have a good trip!

forms: literally: let the devil take it

examples.en: Forget the problems, to hell with all of them!

note: «нека га ђаво носи» is the same about a person or thing; colloq.

examples.en: Call an ambulance!

note: In Serbia the emergency number is 194; often shortened to just «хитна».

examples.en: I don't feel well, I need to sit down.

note: Used to talk about how you feel; «лоше се осећам» - I feel bad.

examples.en: I've had a runny nose for two days now.

meanings: a bigger or smaller size (in a shop)

examples.en: Do you have a bigger size?

note: «број» is a shoe or clothing size; «боја» is color: «у другој боји».

meanings: let me know, just ask (said by a shop assistant)
forms: literally: get in touch with me

examples.en: If you need anything, just let me know.
Fancy a beer? My treat.

note: Said with a question intonation: «може + noun» offers something to drink or eat: «може кафа?».

forms: literally: are you for a coffee?

examples.sr: [Да ли си за ка̏фу]? Спремио сам нову.
examples.en: Want a coffee? I just made a fresh pot.

note: With «вама» (formal): «да ли сте за кафу?»

examples.sr: Нисам прошао, али [ви̏ше сре̏ће дру̏гӣ пу̑т].
examples.en: I didn't pass, but better luck next time.

meanings: things aren't going well for us
forms: literally: it doesn't go for us

examples.sr: Видим да [нам не и̏де] с овим послом.
examples.en: I can see this job isn't going well for us.

examples.sr: Да ли ти се свиђа? - [А јо̏ш ка̀ко]!
examples.en: Do you like it? - You bet!

forms: literally: to fall into the water

examples.en: Our plan fell through.

meanings: you shouldn't have (on getting a gift)

examples.en: Oh, you shouldn't have!

note: A polite reaction to a gift; also «Што сте се трошили?» - why did you go to the expense.

examples.en: You got the color just right!

note: About a gift: the size, the color, the choice itself.

meanings: a heart of gold, a kind soul
forms: literally: a soul of a person

examples.sr: Он је [ду̏ша од чо̏века], свима помаже.
examples.en: He has a heart of gold, he helps everyone.

forms: literally: to be by the will

examples.en: I'm not to your liking.

note: Often negated: «ништа ми није по вољи» - nothing is to my liking.

meanings: nothing is good enough for him, he is never satisfied

examples.sr: [Ни̏шта јој нѝје до̀бро], стално се жали.
examples.en: Nothing is good enough for her, she complains all the time.

meanings: to put everything at stake, to risk everything
forms: literally: to put everything on the die

examples.sr: Дао је све на [ко̏цку] и отворио фирму.
examples.en: He risked everything and started a company.

note: «Коцка» here is a die. The idiom is close to English to stake everything.

examples.en: Wait, I'm coming!

note: Said when you have just arrived or are about to. Similar: «ето га» - here he is.

examples.en: He almost fell off the chair.
The train is about to arrive.

note: Refers to the future or the past: in the first case «any moment now», in the second «it almost happened».

examples.en: Let me help you.
Let me tell you something.

note: A polite opener when offering help. But «само да вам кажем нешто» can also lead into a lecture.

examples.sr: [Не са̏мо] да је закаснио, него је и заборавио књиге.
examples.en: Not only was he late, he also forgot the books.

note: After «него и» the verb stays in its usual form. «не само ... већ и» is also possible.

meanings: how are you, how are things
forms: literally: how are you to me

examples.en: Hi, how are you?

note: The short «ми» makes the question warmer.

examples.en: I'm bored at the lecture.

note: An impersonal construction with «ми». «Досадан си» about a person - you are annoying or boring.

meanings: a roof over one's head, a place to live
forms: literally: a roof over the head

examples.sr: Најважније је да имамо [кро̑в над гла́во̄м].
examples.en: The most important thing is that we have a roof over our heads.

meanings: I don't know, I'm not sure, who knows

examples.sr: Да ли ће доћи? [Шта̏ ја̏ зна̑м].
examples.en: Will he come? I don't know.

note: An evasive answer instead of a direct «не знам»; it sounds softer and vaguer.

examples.en: Who knows whether he'll come.

note: Said about other people's actions or an uncertain future: it is unclear how a person will behave.

forms: literally: from where do I know

examples.en: How should I know where he went?

note: Often with a touch of irritation. A variant is «како ја знам».

examples.sr: Видимо се у лето, [а̏ко Бо̑г да].
examples.en: We'll see each other in the summer, God willing.

note: Even non-believers say it about plans and hopes. It can replace a vague «не знам».

meanings: I'm not really up for it
forms: literally: I'm not quite for that

examples.sr: Да идемо на кишу? [Ни́сам ба̏ш за то̑].
examples.en: Shall we go out in the rain? I'm not really up for it.

note: A soft refusal without a direct «нећу».

meanings: let me see, let me check

examples.en: Let me see if I have any.

note: A shop assistant or anyone else buys time this way to check something.

examples.en: Shall we go? We'll see.

note: A polite way not to answer right away when you don't want to say no.

meanings: nice to meet you, pleased to meet you

examples.en: Nice to meet you, I'm Ana.

note: Said on meeting someone; «мени је драго» adds emphasis. The reply is «и мени».

meanings: what seems to be the problem

examples.en: Good afternoon, what seems to be the problem?

note: A standard question from a doctor or pharmacist.

meanings: to have blood taken for a test

examples.sr: Сутра идем да [ва̏дим кр̑в] на анализу.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to have blood taken for a test.

note: For a test it is «вадити крв»; for donating, «дати крв» is more common.

examples.en: I'll transfer you the money today.

note: Colloquial for a transfer to an account. «Паре» - money, always plural.

examples.en: We didn't want to come by car.

note: «Колима» is the instrumental of «кола». Likewise: «ићи бусом», «авионом».

examples.en: He works with a speech therapist because of a speech impediment.
The baby was born by cesarean section.

note: The name is linked to the Roman emperor, hence «царски». This is what it is called in hospitals.

forms: literally: it set off for me

examples.en: Hurry, it's started!

note: Colloquial for the start of labor. Without «ми» the phrase just means «it got going».

forms: literally: we congratulate on the addition

examples.en: Congratulations on the new arrival!

note: The standard congratulation to new parents. The construction is «честитати на + loc.».

examples.en: Happy Serbian New Year, friends!

note: A greeting on the night of January 14, when the New Year is celebrated by the Julian calendar.

meanings: I care, it matters to me
forms: literally: it has stopped for me

examples.en: I care about you.

note: The construction is «стало ми је до + gen.»: «до тебе», «до посла». Used about what someone holds dear.

examples.en: He's still a mama's boy.

note: About a child who likes to cuddle and gets spoiled. Said of an adult, it can sound like a mild reproach.

examples.en: Enough is enough! Let's go home.

note: A sharp remark when your patience has run out.

examples.en: I give up, I can't take it anymore.

note: Both about physical and emotional exhaustion.

examples.en: It's raining outside.

note: Likewise «пада снег». The verb «ићи» is not used here.

examples.en: It's already dark, let's go home.

forms: literally: it fell on my mind

examples.sr: [Па̏ло ми је на па̏ме̄т] да позовем Ану.
examples.en: It occurred to me to call Ana.

note: Negated: «није ми пало на памет» - it never even crossed my mind.

forms: literally: of my mother to me

examples.en: I saw him, I swear on my mother!

note: An oath in conversation: «мајке ми», «бога ми», «живота ми». They sound emotional, not always serious.

examples.en: Word of honor, I'll come tomorrow.
I'm one hundred percent sure.

note: Colloquial «посто» instead of «одсто»; «сто посто!» - exactly.

examples.en: I'm telling you seriously, don't go there.

note: A variant is «стварно ти кажем».

examples.en: I'm not kidding, he left.

note: Colloq. A variant is «не шалим се».

examples.en: A state of emergency has been declared in the country.
The child has chickenpox.
When it's cold, stay home.

note: The slogan of the 2020 quarantine and the title of a song.

examples.en: Don't worry, this too shall pass.
The children are watching a cartoon.

note: Colloquially «цртач». Only cartoons are dubbed in Serbia; other films have subtitles.

examples.en: Oh, you shouldn't have! Thank you so much.

note: What you say on getting a gift. Also: «што сте се трошили», «нисте морали», «баш сте погодили».

meanings: nowhere in sight, not on the horizon
forms: literally: not even on the emergence

examples.en: The end of the crisis is nowhere in sight.
A vacation is still nowhere in sight.

note: «Помол» is something just appearing over the horizon. Usually negated: «није на помолу».

meanings: he doesn't joke around, don't mess with him
forms: literally: there is no joke with him

examples.sr: Пази шта причаш, [нѐма ша̏ле са њи̑м].
examples.en: Watch what you say, he doesn't joke around.

note: Related: «без шале» - no kidding, seriously; «шалим се» - I'm joking.

meanings: toned and fit (about a woman's figure)

examples.en: After training she is toned and fit.

note: One of the compliments to a woman; also «изгледа као авион» - looks great.

forms: literally: looks like a million dollars

examples.en: You look like a million bucks today.

meanings: a woman who does it all, superwoman

examples.sr: Ради, гради кућу и васпитава децу: права [жѐна зма̏ј].
examples.en: She works, builds a house and raises children: a real superwoman.

note: A compliment of admiration. Similar praise: «права мачка», «лепа као лутка».

examples.en: Sort it out, the sooner the better.
Come as soon as possible.

note: «Што» + a comparative or adverb gives «as ... as possible»: «што брже», «што гласније».

forms: literally: so that I don't jinx it

examples.en: Everything is going well, knock on wood.

note: A variant is «да не чује зло». Serbs knock on wood and say «пу, пу, пу».

examples.en: - Are you going to the game? - You bet!

note: «Него шта мислиш?» - what do you think? Just «Него?» - what else?

meanings: here I am (the usual answer to «Где си?»)

examples.en: - Where are you? - Here I am!
- Where are the keys? - Here they are.

note: «Где си?» is often just a greeting, not a question about place. You can answer «Где си ти?» or «Ево ме!». Same forms: ево те, ево га, ево је, ево нас, ево вас, ево их.

meanings: tongue twister for the syllabic R
forms: literally: on top of the hill a willow sways

examples.sr: Реци брзо: [на вр̏х бр̏да вр́ба мр̏да].
examples.en: Say it fast: on top of the hill a willow sways.

note: It trains the «р» between consonants: врх, брда, врба, мрда. The «р» can be stretched out like a tiger's growl.

meanings: I can't be bothered, I'm too lazy

examples.en: I can't be bothered to cook.
Today I can't be bothered to do anything.

note: «Мрзим» means I hate; «мрзи ме + да + present» is an impersonal laziness.

examples.en: Don't tell me you were late again!

note: A short reaction of surprise, like «Стварно?!» and «Озбиљно?!».

key: phr:то су за мене шпанска села
forms: literally: that is Spanish villages for me

examples.en: Math is all Greek to me.

note: «Шпанска села» means something incomprehensible.

forms: literally: precise as a Swiss watch

examples.en: He is as punctual as a Swiss watch.

meanings: a moment of losing one's temper

examples.sr: Ухватила га је [жу̏та мину́та] и све је разбио.
examples.en: He lost his temper and smashed everything.
Come as soon as possible.

note: «Што + comparative» means «as ... as possible»: што више, што боље, што брже.

examples.en: The faster, the better, they're waiting for us.

meanings: to mix up unrelated things, to mix apples and oranges
forms: literally: to mix grannies and frogs

examples.sr: Не [ме̏шај ба́бе̄ и жа̀бе], то су два посла.
examples.en: Don't mix apples and oranges, those are two separate jobs.

meanings: a guest soon wears out his welcome
forms: literally: for every guest three days are enough

examples.sr: [Сва̏ког го̏ста три̏ да̀на до̏ста], па су отишли.
examples.en: Three days are enough for any guest, so they left.

note: A proverb about hospitality: a guest is welcome only for a short time.

meanings: kind words can get you far
forms: literally: a kind word opens iron doors

examples.sr: [Ле̏па ре̑ч гво̀здена вра́та о̀твара], пробај љубазно.
examples.en: A kind word opens iron doors, try being polite.

key: phr:први кучићи се у воду бацају
forms: literally: the first puppies are thrown into the water

examples.sr: Не брини, [пр̏ви ку̏чићи се у во̏ду ба̀цају].
examples.en: Don't worry, the first attempt rarely goes well.

note: A first experience is often a failure; it is made as a trial.

meanings: if you won't do it the nice way, you'll do it the hard way
forms: literally: if you don't want it kindly, you'll want it by force

examples.sr: [А̏ко не̑ће̄ш ми̏лом, хо̀ћеш си̏ло̄м], ја одлучујем.
examples.en: If you won't do it the nice way, you'll do it the hard way, I'm the one who decides.

examples.sr: Не треба [у̀зимати здра̏во за го̀тово] све што чујеш.
examples.en: You shouldn't take everything you hear for granted.

note: «Здраво за готово» - accepting something without checking it.

meanings: a friend in need is a friend indeed, true character shows in hard times
forms: literally: in hardship heroes are recognized

examples.sr: [На му̏ци се по̀знају ју̏наци], видећемо ко ће остати.
examples.en: True character shows in hard times, we'll see who stays.

meanings: ultimately, at the end of the day

examples.en: At the end of the day, the decision is yours.

forms: literally: a suit doesn't make the man

examples.sr: [Оде́ло не чѝни чо̏века], он је добар.
examples.en: Clothes don't make the man, he's a good guy.

meanings: very good-looking, pretty as a doll

examples.en: You look as pretty as a doll today.

note: In Serbia you can compliment a man's looks too, not only a woman's. Colloq. variant: леп ко лутка.

examples.en: You look nice today.

note: With «ми» it adds warmth: «лепо ми изгледаш». Polite form: «лепо изгледате». «Добро» can replace «лепо».

examples.sr: Каже да је његова другарица [до̀бра ри̏ба].
examples.en: He says his friend is a real catch.

note: Men's slang about a girl in the third person. A similar one is «мачка».

examples.en: May I ask a question?
I have to book an appointment with the dentist.
We have to make a decision by Friday.
The government took measures against overcrowding.
Tomorrow I'll submit a visa application.
The hotel provides an airport transfer service.

meanings: to get through an illness (in bed)
forms: literally: to lie through an illness

examples.en: He got through the flu without any medication.

note: About an illness that you sit out in bed.

meanings: to be in prison, to serve time

examples.en: He spent a long time in prison.

forms: literally: to carry off a victory

examples.en: Our team won the victory.

forms: literally: to live through a defeat

examples.en: The national team suffered a defeat.
The schoolgirl won first place.
The director will give a speech.
I've been on a diet for a month now.

forms: literally: to break through a deadline

examples.en: Unfortunately, we missed the deadline.
I've been to Serbia several times.

note: The comparative here compares nothing: it means «several», not «more».

examples.sr: Не можемо да дођемо [из ви̏ше ра̀злога].
examples.en: We can't come for several reasons.

meanings: for a long time, for a longer stay

examples.en: I'm going to Russia for a long stay.
The apartment is for rent short-term.
My grandmother's hearing isn't very good.

note: A soft way to say «badly»: «мало слабије говорим српски».

examples.en: This film is relatively recent.
I'm looking for a shorter book.
Are you planning a vacation in the near future?

meanings: like a wind-up toy (about fast chatter)

examples.en: The little girl talks like a wind-up toy.

note: «Навијен» comes from «навити» (to wind a spring or a clock). The form follows the gender: «као навијена», «као навијен».

meanings: at full speed, a mile a minute

examples.en: She talks a mile a minute.

note: Often about fast speech. «Сат» is an hour, as in kilometers per hour.

examples.en: Hi, how's it going?

forms: literally: there is nothing for what

examples.en: Thank you! - You're welcome.
Achoo! - Bless you!

note: Said after a sneeze. You reply with «хвала».

examples.en: It's a deal, an agreement is an agreement.

examples.sr: [Без бри̏ге], све ће бити у реду.
examples.en: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
Thanks for the help, all the best!
Thanks, and the same to you!

note: Said both before a meal (enjoy your meal) and when parting. Not to be confused with «пријатно ми је» - I'm pleased.

examples.en: He is a true hero through and through.

note: An ironic, colloq. intensification of «прави».

examples.sr: Донела си ми кафу, [ти си пра̏ва]!
examples.en: You brought me coffee, you're a star!

note: To a woman after a nice, unexpected gesture; to a man: «ти си прав».

key: phr:на које име да оставим сто
meanings: what name shall I put the table under?

examples.sr: Добар дан, [на ко̀је̄ и̏ме да о̀ставим сто̑]?
examples.en: Good afternoon, what name shall I put the table under?

note: A phrase of the restaurant host; the reply: «Резервисано је».

meanings: I would like to reserve a table

examples.sr: Добар дан, [хте̏ла бих да резѐрвишем сто̑] за вечерас.
examples.en: Good afternoon, I would like to reserve a table for tonight.

note: A man says «хтео бих». On sunny weekends you may be left without a table if you don't book.

meanings: to get a beating, to get a hiding

examples.en: If you don't stop, you'll get a hiding.

meanings: am I hurting you? (when combing hair)
forms: literally: am I tugging at you?

examples.en: Am I hurting you?

meanings: how much do I owe you?

examples.en: Thanks, how much do I owe you?

note: A man says «колико сам вам дужан».

meanings: I would like to get my ends trimmed

examples.sr: [Хте̏ла бих да о̀шишам кра̏јеве], само мало.
examples.en: I would like to get my ends trimmed, just a little.

note: A man says «хтео бих». For coloring: «хтела бих да офарбам косу».

examples.en: Let's blow-dry it into curls.

note: Other options: «на равно» (straight), «на таласе» (waves).

meanings: to hold the door for someone

examples.en: He kindly held the door for me.

note: «Врата» is neuter plural; придржим, придржиш.

examples.en: Press the button and call the elevator.
First knock on the door, then come in.

note: «Позвонити на врата» - to ring the doorbell.

examples.en: My husband is celebrating his double coming of age.

note: A joke about the age of 36: 18 times 2.

meanings: long may he live, long may she live (birthday song)

examples.en: Long may he live, long may he live, and may he be happy!
Long may she live, long may she live, and may she be happy!

note: In the song «Диван дан» the form follows the gender of the birthday person: «живео» (he), «живела» (she). Don't mix it up with «живело» - neuter.

meanings: that won't do you any good
forms: literally: that isn't good for you

examples.sr: Превише си поносан, [не ва̏ља ти то̑].
examples.en: You're too proud, that won't do you any good.
He did the job properly.

meanings: it would be a good idea to, you ought to

examples.en: You ought to change the tires.

meanings: it is proper to, it is the done thing

examples.en: We should visit our aunt, it's the done thing.

note: A social «ought»: that is how it is done, it is expected.

examples.en: It's no use, they don't want to listen.
It's cheap, it's worth a try.
Come here, sit on my lap.

note: «Крило» also means a wing; «у крилу» - on the lap.

meanings: it's like talking to a wall
forms: literally: as if I'm talking to a wall

examples.sr: [Ка̏о да при̏чам зи̏ду], никад не слуша.
examples.en: It's like talking to a wall, he never listens.

forms: literally: you will remember my words

examples.sr: [Запа̀мтићеш мо̏је ре̏чи], још ће ти требати.
examples.en: Mark my words, you'll still need it.

meanings: you will do as I say
forms: literally: you have to listen to me

examples.sr: [И̏ма да ме слу̏шаш], јер сам ти мајка.
examples.en: You'll do as I say, because I'm your mother.

note: A strict demand: «има да» + present. A parent says it when losing patience.

key: phr:на главу си ми се попео
meanings: you're driving me up the wall (nagging)
forms: literally: you climbed onto my head

examples.sr: [На гла̑ву си ми се по̀пео] са том игрицом!
examples.en: You're driving me up the wall with that game!

note: Colloquial and irritated; said to a child who keeps demanding something.

forms: literally: you have no more credit with me

examples.sr: [Нѐмаш ви̏ше креди́та ко̑д ме̏не], лагао си.
examples.en: You've lost my trust, you lied.
I'd rather stay home.

meanings: I'm upset, I feel bad about it

examples.sr: Много [ми је кри̑во] што ниси дошла.
examples.en: I'm really upset that you didn't come.

examples.sr: [До̀садило ми је] да чекам у реду.
examples.en: I'm fed up with waiting in line.

forms: literally: it pours as if from a bucket

examples.en: It's pouring outside.
It looks like the weather is turning bad.

note: The opposite: «време се пролепшава» (improves), «разведрава се» (clears up).

examples.en: Nice weather is forecast for the weekend.
Child, tuck your shirt in, it's chilly.

note: Typical motherly care: it is cold, your back must be covered. One of the most common phrases of Serbian mothers.

examples.en: When you finish showering, turn off the water heater.

meanings: to put oneself in someone's shoes
forms: literally: to put oneself in someone's place

examples.sr: Покушај да [се ста̏виш на њѐгово ме̏сто].
examples.en: Try to put yourself in his shoes.
We turned into a dead end.

note: Also figuratively: a hopeless situation.

meanings: shall we go, let's get going

examples.en: Are you ready? Shall we go?
Let me see what you wrote.

meanings: shall I make you a coffee? (an offer)
forms: literally: that I cook you coffee

examples.en: Shall I make you a coffee?

note: «Да» + present instead of an infinitive in offers: «Да те зовем касније?» - shall I call you later?

forms: literally: that it were for me to know

examples.sr: [Да ми је зна̏ти] где је сада.
examples.en: If only I knew where he is now.

note: «Да ми је» + infinitive is a wistful «if only». From the song «Липе цвату».

key: phr:нека ти се све жеље испуне
meanings: may all your wishes come true

examples.en: May all your wishes come true!
Take a deep breath and hold it.
Hold your breath for three seconds.
Straighten your back and lower your shoulders.

meanings: what do you do in your free time?

examples.en: What do you do in your free time?
- Are you Angelina? - That's right.

examples.sr: Мислио сам да ће бити досадно, али [ба̏ш су̀протно].
examples.en: I thought it would be boring, but quite the opposite.

examples.sr: Знала сам да ћеш се наљутити, [ба̏ш за̀то̄] ти нисам рекла.
examples.en: I knew you'd get angry, that's exactly why I didn't tell you.

meanings: shoo, kitty (said to someone who sneezed)

examples.en: Achoo! - Bless you! - Thanks.

note: What Serbs say when someone sneezes, especially to children. The neutral variant is «наздравље».

meanings: a loose tongue, a big mouth

examples.sr: Не верујем му, он има [јѐзик без дла̏ке].
examples.en: I don't trust him, he has a loose tongue.

note: About a chatterbox who says whatever comes to mind.

examples.sr: Није идеално, али [та̀ко̄ је, ка̀ко је].
examples.en: It's not ideal, but it is what it is.

note: A philosophical shrug: the situation can't be changed, you just accept it. Often followed by «шта ћеш».

examples.sr: - Опет касниш! - [Па шта̏ да ра̏дим], гужва је.
examples.en: - You're late again! - What can I do, there's traffic.

note: A shrug: it doesn't depend on me. A short excuse.

meanings: just a moment; excuse me (to get past)

examples.sr: [Са̏мо ма̏ло], молим вас, излазим на следећој.
examples.en: Excuse me, please, I'm getting off at the next stop.

note: A polite request to wait or to be let through: on a bus, in a shop, when you need to squeeze past. Similar: «само тренутак», «само минут».

examples.en: If the boss finds out about this, I'm done for.

note: Figurative «готов»: it's all over for the person. For ordinary readiness, use «спреман сам».

meanings: it's too late now, nothing can be done

examples.en: Don't fret, there's nothing to be done now.

note: What is done cannot be undone. A short «...и готово» can end a phrase: and that's it.

examples.en: Come in, welcome!

note: Said by a host, e.g. at a Slava (a family patron saint's feast). Guests reply with a wish: «срећна слава, домаћине».

examples.sr: Шеф је отишао на [слу̏жбенӣ пу̑т] у Беч.
examples.en: The boss went on a business trip to Vienna.

note: A set phrase: «ићи на службени пут». Also: «пут у иностранство» - a trip abroad.

meanings: if only, would that it were so

examples.en: If only that were so!

note: Expresses regret about what is not so, with «да» + past tense. Bookish and used in songs, e.g. «Јесен у мени»: «камо среће да сам пјеват могао».

meanings: better to be drunk than old

examples.sr: Знаш шта кажу: [бо̏ље̄ би̏ти пѝјан не̏го ста̏р].
examples.en: You know what they say: better to be drunk than old.

note: A line from a well-known song by the band Плави оркестар.

meanings: which stop should I get off at

examples.sr: Извините, [на ко̀јо̄ј ста̏ници да ѝзађем] за Нови Београд?
examples.en: Excuse me, which stop should I get off at for New Belgrade?

note: A question to the driver or a fellow passenger. Similar: «који бус иде до...?» (which bus goes to...) and «где треба да изађем?».

meanings: until what time is it open

examples.en: Until what time is this pharmacy open?

note: The subject can be left out: «До колико сати радите?» - until what time are you open?

examples.sr: Да ли ће све бити у реду? - [Бо̏же здра̏вља]!
examples.en: Will everything be all right? - Let's hope so!

note: A wish that what is needed comes true. «Боже здравља» is also heard as an exclamation in the song «In Corpore Sano» by Konstrakta.

meanings: I want to open an account

examples.sr: [Же̏лим да о̀творим ра̀чӯн] у вашој банци.
examples.en: I want to open an account at your bank.

note: A polite variant: «хтео бих да отворим рачун». Specify the type: «девизни» (foreign currency), «штедни» (savings), «текући» (current).

examples.en: I want to withdraw five hundred euros.

note: «Подићи новац» - to withdraw cash, «уплатити новац» - to deposit it into an account. ATM - «банкомат».

examples.en: I forgot my online banking password.

note: A woman says «заборавила сам». Instead of «лозинка» you can say «шифра» (code) or «пин картице».

key: phr:да ли је оглас још увек актуелан

examples.sr: Добар дан, [да ли је о̏гла̄с јо̏ш у̏ве̄к а̏ктуе̄лан]?
examples.en: Good afternoon, is the ad still current?

note: The first question when calling about a rental ad. Next: «зовем у вези са вашим огласом на сајту» - I'm calling about your ad on the site.

examples.sr: [Да ли је ста̑н на̏мештен] и има ли клима-уређај?
examples.en: Is the apartment furnished, and does it have air conditioning?

note: «Намештен» - furnished; «ненамештен» - empty. Next you ask about heating («грејање») and the number of rooms («број соба»).

key: phr:треба ми мало времена да размислим
meanings: I need a little time to think

examples.sr: Хвала, [тре́ба ми ма̏ло врѐмена да размѝслим].
examples.en: Thank you, I need a little time to think.

note: A polite way not to decide at once, e.g. at an apartment viewing; short: «треба да размислим».

examples.sr: На вратима пише: [«Ми то̑ не при̏мамо»].
examples.en: The sign on the door says: "We don't accept that."

note: A sign in government offices. A pun: «ми то» sounds like «Мито» - a bribe, so «we don't accept bribes».

examples.en: Do you have something to calm the nerves?

note: «За» + acc. gives the purpose: «нешто за кашаљ», «нешто за спавање». For an illness, «против» is used: «лек против главобоље».

examples.en: Everything is done perfectly.

note: A rhyming expression: the work is done flawlessly, nothing is left to finish.

examples.en: They bought a house, a car, the whole lot.

note: From the Italian «tutto completo». Said when listing everything in full, or for «all inclusive».

meanings: boasting about one's possessions and business

examples.sr: Прича о [авѝонима-камѝонима], а нема ни динара.
examples.en: He talks about planes and trucks, but doesn't have a single dinar.

note: About a person who shows off, talking big about his property and dealings.

examples.en: That's just junk, don't buy it!

note: Unserious business of the «you scratch my back» kind, or goods of poor quality.
